extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, assignees, and patent practitioners preparing or filing U.S. patent term extension (PTE) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing a U.S. patent term extension (35 U.S.C. 156 / 37 CFR 1.740–1.741) application with the USPTO, including required contents, timing, signatures, and supporting showings to establish eligibility and calculate extension length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply (owner or agent)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an extension of the term of a patent under this section, the owner of record of the patent or its agent shall submit an application to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 156(d)(1) and MPEP: application may only be submitted by owner of record or its agent. If filed by assignee(s), refer to reel/frame numbers of recorded assignment. If filed by an agent or registered practitioner not of record, file a power of attorney (limited POA acceptable) and proof of authorization may be required. If applicant was not the marketing applicant, there must have been an agency relationship between patent owner and marketing applicant; obtaining a letter from the marketing applicant authorizing reliance is advisable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application for extension of a patent term must be submitted by the owner of record of the patent or its agent and must comply with the requirements of § 1.740. If the application is submitted by the patent owner, the application must be signed either by the patent owner in compliance with § 3.73(b) or by a registered practitioner on behalf of the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.730(b)-(d): if submitted on behalf of the patent owner by an agent (e.g., licensee), the application must be signed by a registered practitioner on behalf of the agent. The Office may require proof that the agent/practitioner is authorized to act for the patent owner or agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 60‑day filing window (timeliness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Such an application may only be submitted within the sixty-day period beginning on the date the product received permission under the provision of law under which the applicable regulatory review period occurred for commercial marketing or use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory 60-day window is mandatory, not waivable or extendable. The first day of the 60-day period is the approval date (day one), not the day after. Applicants are cautioned to avoid filing on the last day to avoid inadvertent misses. See Unimed and related authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business day and 4:30 P.M. rule for permission date
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of determining the date on which a product receives permission, if such permission is transmitted after 4:30 P.M., Eastern Time, on a business day, or transmitted on a non-business day, the product is deemed to receive such permission on the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business day = Monday–Friday excluding federal holidays under 5 U.S.C. 6103. This affects the start of the 60-day filing window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered date for controlled substance recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: For drug products where the Secretary of HHS intends to recommend controls under the Controlled Substances Act, the drug product shall be considered to have been approved and to have permission for commercial marketing beginning on the 'covered date' (the later of several specified events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 156(i) defines 'covered date' as the later of: (A) approval under specific PHSA/FFDCA provisions, (B) conditional approval under FFDCA §571(b), (C) indexing under §572(d), or (D) issuance of interim final rule controlling the drug under CSA §201(j). The 60-day period for filing PTE begins on the covered date for such drugs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The application under this section, and any related submissions to the Office, must be submitted using the USPTO patent electronic filing system in accordance with the USPTO patent electronic filing system requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(b) and 37 CFR 1.741 emphasize electronic filing via USPTO system; filing date accorded when a complete application is received via that system (or via permitted certificate-of-transmission procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: identification of approved product
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete identification of the approved product as by appropriate chemical and generic name, physical structure or characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(1): Identification must enable the Director to determine whether the patent claims the approved product or a method of using/manufacturing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: identification of federal statute(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete identification of the Federal statute including the applicable provision of law under which the regulatory review occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(2): When regulatory review occurred under more than one statute, list each appropriate statute. PTE will be based on review of the product as either medical device or drug product, not a combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: identification of permission date
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification of the date on which the product received permission for commercial marketing or use under the provision of law under which the applicable regulatory review period occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(3): The date is generally the mailing date of the approval letter. For food additives it's usually the effective date in the regulation; for drugs requiring DEA scheduling the later DEA interim final rule date may control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: active ingredient info for drug products
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a drug product, an identification of each active ingredient in the product and as to each active ingredient, a statement that it has not been previously approved for commercial marketing or use under specified statutes, or a statement of when it was approved, the use, and the provision of law under which it was approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(4): This information is necessary for eligibility determinations, especially where approval is based on a second or subsequent approval of an active ingredient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: statement of timeliness and last filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that the application is being submitted within the sixty day period permitted for submission pursuant to § 1.720(f) and an identification of the date of the last day on which the application could be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(5): Applicant should compute and state the last eligible filing date (account for weekends/holidays/business-day rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: identification of patent for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete identification of the patent for which an extension is being sought by the name of the inventor, the patent number, the date of issue, and the date of expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(6): Expiration date should reflect 35 U.S.C. 154 term, including any patent term adjustment and terminal disclaimers; it's recommended to show how expiration date was calculated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: copy of patent (specification, claims, drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the patent for which an extension is being sought, including the entire specification (including claims) and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(7): Entire patent copy required as part of the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: copy of disclaimers, corrections, reexamination certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, receipt of maintenance fee payment, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(8): Include any documents that affect patent term or claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: statement that patent claims the approved product and listing/showing of applicable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that the patent claims the approved product, or a method of using or manufacturing the approved product, and a showing which lists each applicable patent claim and demonstrates the manner in which at least one such patent claim reads on the approved product, method of use, and/or method of manufacturing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(9): At most a showing explaining three claims is required (one product, one method of use, one method of manufacture) but every claim that claims the approved product/method/manufacture must be listed. Guidance provides examples: use of variables/substituents for generic chemical claims, reference to column/line numbers and drawing refs for means-plus-function claims, and use of an element-by-element claim chart for devices; show relevant equivalents where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: statement of regulatory dates per product type (35 U.S.C.156(g) info)
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the relevant dates and information pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 156(g) to enable HHS or Agriculture to determine the applicable regulatory review period, with specific date types required for different product categories (human drug/biologic, new animal drug, veterinary biological product, food/color additive, medical device).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(10): For human drugs/biologics include IND effective date and number, NDA/PLA submission date and number, NDA approval date; for animal drugs include dates for major tests or exemptions, NADA submission and approval dates; for veterinary biologicals include authority to prepare experimental product date, license application submission date, license issuance date; for food/color additives include major test initiation date, petition submission and Federal Register publication date; for devices include IDE effective date or clinical investigation start date, PMA or PDP submission date and approval date. If no regulatory event clearly reflects testing/approval commencement, applicant should claim dates and provide reasonable bases and substantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: description of marketing applicant activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief description of the significant activities undertaken by the marketing applicant during the applicable regulatory review period with respect to the approved product and the significant dates applicable to such activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(11): Include significant communications with the regulatory agency (e.g., submissions of new data, communications about testing protocols, premarketing requirement discussions). The applicant is not required to establish due diligence; non-substantive/insignificant communications need not be listed. If the marketing applicant is a different entity, show the agency relationship and include only substantive activities; USPTO will not obtain information from the marketing applicant on behalf of the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: statement of claimed eligibility and length of extension with calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that in the opinion of the applicant the patent is eligible for the extension and a statement as to the length of extension claimed, including how the length of extension was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(12): Applicant must show how claimed extension length was calculated and indicate whether statutory caps (14-year or five-year limits under specified subsections) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: duty to disclose material information
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement that applicant acknowledges a duty to disclose to the Director of the USPTO and the Secretary of HHS or Agriculture any information which is material to the determination of entitlement to the extension sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(13): See MPEP §2001.06(e) regarding the duty of disclosure related to regulatory review. Materiality to entitlement must be acknowledged in application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: prescribed fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The prescribed fee for receiving and acting upon the application for extension must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(14): Payment via prescribed fee (see §1.20(j)). Preferable to include authorization to charge a deposit account; alternatively pay via USPTO Financial Manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal application content: correspondence contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The name, address, telephone number, and email address of the person to whom inquiries and correspondence related to the application for patent term extension are to be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(a)(15): USPTO uses this info strictly for PTE correspondence; to change this info file appropriate PTE.POA document. For other patent-file correspondence use 37 CFR 1.33 change-of-address procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application for filing date (37 CFR 1.741): required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete application for filing date purposes must include: identification of the approved product; identification of each Federal statute under which regulatory review occurred; identification of the patent for which an extension is being sought; identification of each claim of the patent which claims the approved product or method of using/manufacturing it; sufficient information to enable the Director and HHS/Ag to determine eligibility, rights derived, and length of regulatory review period; and a brief description of marketing applicant activities and significant dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.741(a)(1)-(6): These requirements are mandated by 35 U.S.C.156 and must be satisfied within the 60-day filing period for establishment of the filing date. The Office will consider statutory requirements satisfied where sufficient information is provided to act on the application even if further information may later be desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal application; correction of informalities and time to correct
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is informal under this section, the Office will so notify the applicant. The applicant has two months from the mail date of the notice, or such time set in the notice, to correct the informality (time may be extended under §1.136 unless notice indicates otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.740(c): If application is held informal, applicant may request review under 1.740(c) or correct the informality. If the application satisfies 37 CFR 1.741 requirements, the filing date can be established even if later held informal under 1.740.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition procedure for review of incompleteness or filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant requests review of a notice that an application is incomplete, or review of the filing date accorded, applicant must file a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in §1.17(f) within two months of the mail date of the notice (time may be extended under §1.136 unless notice indicates otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP: follow the petition procedures and fee requirements; petitions must be timely to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and reporting of patent expiration (account for PTA and disclaimers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The expiration date of the patent for which an extension is sought should be the expiration date according to law (35 U.S.C.154) at the time of filing, and should take into account any patent term adjustment under 35 U.S.C.154(b) as well as any terminal disclaimer; it is recommended the application shows how the expiration date was calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP gives example calculations (e.g., base 20-year-from-filing plus patent term adjustment days) and recommends showing arithmetic used to arrive at expiration date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing how patent claims read on the approved product (claim chart guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The showing should clearly demonstrate how the product, method of use and/or method of manufacture claim reads on the approved product; where appropriate use variables/substituents mapping for generic chemical claims, reference to column/line and drawing numbers for means-plus-function claims, or an element-by-element claim chart for devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP examples: for generic chemical structure claims list variables/substituents corresponding to approved product; for "means for"/112(f) claims reference patent text and drawings and describe equivalents; for medical devices, a claim chart describing element-by-element correspondence is helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTE.POA and limited power of attorney practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO patent electronic filing system includes the document description 'Limited POA and/or Change of Address for a Patent Term Extension Application' (document code PTE.POA) for limited powers of attorney that are filed specifically for patent term extension applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a PTE.POA will not change an existing power for the underlying patent or establish power for the underlying patent; a registered practitioner not of record who files the PTE application is considered acting in a representative capacity in accordance with 37 CFR 1.34. For changes to general patent correspondence addresses, use other document codes and comply with 37 CFR 1.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling of approvals that require DEA scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: For drug products where HHS recommends controls under the Controlled Substances Act, the drug cannot legally be marketed until an interim final rule is published by DEA scheduling the drug; the approval date for PTE purposes will be the later of the FDA approval date(s) or the DEA interim final rule issuance under CSA §201(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP clarifies that for such drugs the 'covered date' may be later than FDA approval; the 60-day filing window begins on the covered date.
